comment: One of my favorite professors @ UR.

Prof Kapanga makes the class fun and is a very generous grader. There were blog responses due every class with readings, as well as 3 mini essays (4 pages), a full essay (6 pages) for the final, and an in-class midterm. He will cold call in a friendly way even if you participate a lot. He's not tech savvy, but he is available to meet.

Prof. Kapanga is a great person and teacher. He has a great sense of humor to make class fun and engaging. Since it meets every day, there was homework assigned each night, but it was never hard to complete. He is also a very fair grader. Definitely would take again.
Absolutely adore him! He is such a sweet human being. Not the best teacher, but he tries his best and really wants his students to succeed. I highly recommend his class!

Absolute amazing person. Enthralling conversations in French. Not a tough grader and very willing to work with you to get the grade you want. This class is much easier if you have previous French experience and parts will feel like review however it is also very manageable if you aren't confident in your french skills. 11/10 would take again.

Professor Kapanga is so kind and caring. The assessments are manageable and he's also flexible with deadlines if you ask. Readings are very long and class is harder to keep up with if you didn't do the homework. I loved the course material as well. I would definitely take another class with this professor

Solid professor, gives good feedback, accessible and responds to emails fast. A bit disorganized and class can lose focus sometimes. A lot of reading but he is willing to adjust the schedule to students. No tests, but several papers. Not a really harsh grader. Really cares about what he is teaching and you can tell he is passionate about it.

Great professor! He gives lots of reading and can be disorganized when giving assignments, which was frustrating, but he was good at making sure we were caught up in each class. He will cold call you, but not in a way that makes class stressful as he keeps the atmosphere casual and fun. It was nice to have a prof so passionate and knowledgeable.

Dr. Kapanga is a kind and caring professor. He assigns lots of reading much of which is very confusing, however, class discussions make the readings easier to understand. He will randomly call on you a lot. His tests are hard but he is a pretty generous grader. If you skim the readings, show up, and participate, then you will do well in his class.

Directions are extremely poorly communicated and written. Nearly impossible to understand lectures, prompts, and exams. For an FYS, possibly your worst choice. Countless dense readings that are never cleared up, and exams are confusing. If you dont read, youre screwed. If you read, youre still probably screwed

PROS: Dr. Kapanga is a brilliant guy, no question about it. He captures interest in 9 AM lectures, which is no small feat. CONS: Though a genius, Dr. Kapanga dumbs down his lectures. He tries to engage the class without actually letting us alter the discussion, so many don't participate. Grades unforgivingly YOU WILL BE EXPOSED, SO READ and u fine.
nice professor and interesting class if you actually do the assigned readings.

Do not take his FYS. Hes a nice person but I wouldnt take his class again. He is a tough grader which is fine but hes not clear about what his grading criteria is. His questions are often long and convoluted. When he does leave comments, and doesnt just take off points by threes, you cant read them.

There is a short essay due every week, but that is the only thing he grades you on. A lot of people didn't even come to class most days. Very disorganized; even I have no idea what we did over the semester, but it was easy and in French so hopefully I learned something! Very nice guy but the class is boring.
One of the best professors I've had at UR. Took his FYS last spring and had a blast. As long as you try you'll get a B+ or an A-
While I got a bit bored in this class, I truly appreciated the fact that he was helpfum outside class.

Not sure why he got average reviews, but he's a great teacher. It's an easy grade and everyone in the class does well (it's pretty much impossible not to) but you still learn a ton. Work is really minimal especially considering it's a 221 class. Tests are pretty easy. Highly recommended.

Really nice, not always the easiest to follow in class but you figure out how to work with it. Tests get easier. Sometimes his grading makes absolutely no sense but everyone seemed to end up with good grades. He is from Africa so if you randomly bring up things about Africa he will love you. The drill sections that go with the course are helpful.

Amazing teacher. He is very smart, seems to know a lot about what he's teaching. He's a very kind-hearted man who wants all his students to do well but who also expects his students to work hard. He didn't seem disorganized to me, he just gets too involved in what he's teaching. If you work hard and are interested in his class you can get an A.
not good. drop now. impossible grader. dont know how he is for languages but i assure you that you want to have someone else explain to you enlightenment literature

He's SO disorganized and his grading system is really unfair and annoying.  In class, he tends to ramble and even though he's nice and occasionally funny, I feel like I'm not learning very much and I'm often confused as to the assignments and what in the world we are doing. He's not terrible, but if you have another option, choose them.

Love this man! He is SO sweet. He did an amazing job of keeping my class entertained, despite the fact that it was a five-days a week class @ 8:15 am...I'd say his class was fairly easy, he doesn't try to trick you at the very least- pretty straightforward. But, if you don't know your conjugations and grammar, you might be screwed on the tests.

Very kind, joking teacher...considering this was a 2 unit course very light on the homework although he graded it hard.  Tests were graded very easily except for the oral sections.  Excellent at teaching oral skills in class, but never really lectured on grammar and vocabulary.
He was a great professor! He knew so much about the topics that it made class very interesting. He's fair with grading. His knowledge on french is incredible.
Nice enough guy, but not at all knowledgeable about his subject.  I was embarrassed for him.
Excellent professor, very clear and helpful. Highly recommended!
Nice guy, but not very organized.  I don't recommend him for upper level French.

Really nice guy and a native French speaker. Genuinely wants his students to do well. Lots of focus on pronunciation and speaking which is really helpful. The tests come with no suprises. If you follow the class and study the chapter the tests should be easy.

He is a really good French professor if you want to continue with French beyoun elementary and intermediate; there are easier options otherwise. He is a native speaker so he stressed on pronunciation. His classes go by really fast even the Tuesday, Thursday ones!
